verdict: keep, narrowly, and delete half of it the moment a dependency is allowed
what_ours_does: Two unrelated files that share a directory because both repair the Windows side of a WSL session. make_lane_logos.py writes four 256x256 RGBA PNGs of a single letter, by hand: zlib for the IDAT stream, struct for chunk framing, binascii.crc32 for checksums, and a 5x7 bitmap font typed into the source. fix-kitty-launchers.ps1 rewrites two Windows .lnk files to launch kitty through wslg.exe instead of wsl.exe, and flips byte 21 of the ShellLinkHeader to set the run-as-admin flag.
why: The PNG half is only defensible because of a measured absence, not because hand-rolling a PNG encoder is a good idea. Pillow is not installed in this distro and neither is ImageMagick, both checked 2026-08-01, and the repo's standing convention is stdlib-only tools under tools/. Given that constraint the entire encoder is about forty lines and removes a dependency argument; without that constraint Pillow wins outright and this file should be deleted, which is why the recheck below is a one-line install test rather than a design review. The .lnk half is different and does not have an off-the-shelf answer: WScript.Shell, which is the standard scripted way to write a shortcut and is what this file uses for everything else, cannot set the run-as-admin flag at all. That flag lives in a single bit of the binary header and every tool listed below either omits it or wraps the same byte edit. So the byte-21 write is not a shortcut taken around a library, it is the thing no library exposes.

alternatives.name: Pillow (PIL)
alternatives.covers: All of make_lane_logos.py, in about five lines with ImageDraw and a real font.
alternatives.gap: Not installed here, and adding it makes tools/ no longer stdlib-only. Nothing else in tools/ has a third-party import.
alternatives.cost: pip install pillow, permissive HPND licence.
alternatives.maturity: Mature, the default answer for Python raster work.

alternatives.name: ImageMagick convert / magick
alternatives.covers: The same four PNGs from a shell one-liner with -pointsize and -annotate.
alternatives.gap: Not installed, and it is a system package rather than a Python dependency, so it moves the problem from the manifest to the host image.

alternatives.name: cairosvg
alternatives.covers: Letter glyphs as SVG rasterised to PNG, with real typography instead of a 5x7 bitmap.
alternatives.gap: Pulls in cairo and its native libs, much heavier than the job. Overkill for four single-character watermarks.

alternatives.name: matplotlib savefig
alternatives.covers: Text rendered to a transparent PNG.
alternatives.gap: A plotting library used as a text rasteriser, and the alpha and exact-pixel control this needs are awkward through its API.
alternatives.cost: Already a transitive dependency in some subprojects, not in this one.

alternatives.name: pylnk3
alternatives.covers: Reading and writing Windows .lnk files from Python, which would replace the WScript.Shell half of fix-kitty-launchers.ps1 and let the whole thing be Python.
alternatives.gap: Does not expose the run-as-admin header bit either, so the byte edit stays. It would also mean driving a Windows shell object from a Linux interpreter across the WSL boundary.

alternatives.name: WScript.Shell COM alone
alternatives.covers: Target, arguments, working directory, icon, window style. Already used here for exactly those.
alternatives.gap: No property for the elevation flag. This is the documented limitation that forces the byte-21 write and is the whole reason the script is longer than a one-liner.

alternatives.name: NirSoft nircmd shortcut
alternatives.covers: Creating shortcuts from a command line, including some properties.
alternatives.gap: Third-party closed-source binary, frequently flagged by endpoint protection, and still no elevation flag.

alternatives.name: New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink
alternatives.covers: Nothing here. Listed because it is the obvious PowerShell answer to 'make a link' and it is the wrong one.
alternatives.gap: A symlink is not a shortcut and carries no arguments, icon, working directory, or elevation flag. It cannot launch wslg.exe with a command line.

evidence: Absence of both raster libraries measured on this host 2026-08-01: python3 -c 'import PIL' raises ModuleNotFoundError and `which convert magick` returns nothing. The four generated PNGs were verified by decoding rather than by the write not raising: signature bytes plus IHDR geometry, and the ink pixel counts came back 14112/15680/10192/14112, matching the 5x7 glyph masks exactly. The watermark path was proven to rasterise rather than merely parse by a discriminating test: a bad --logo path raises FileNotFoundError from kitty/render_cache.py while a good path is silent. On the launcher half, the root cause it repairs was proven from /proc/114950/exe and its argv, not from reading config: the taskbar pin invoked a bare `kitty`, PATH resolved that to /usr/bin/kitty 0.32.2, and ~/.config/kitty/kitty.conf had been written against 0.48.2, which is why 51 options were being silently dropped and DECSET 2031 errored.
recheck: Run `python3 -c 'import PIL'`. The moment that exits 0, or the moment any third-party import is permitted under tools/, delete make_lane_logos.py's hand-rolled png() and render() and rewrite them against Pillow: roughly 40 of the 353 lines survive. The .lnk half needs a different trigger: recheck whether any maintained library has exposed the ShellLinkHeader elevation bit as a first-class property, and if one has, replace the byte-21 write with it.
strongest_counterargument: That a hand-written PNG encoder in a repo whose whole subject is verification is exactly the kind of thing this gate exists to stop, and 'the library is not installed' is a circular defence because installing it is one command. That argument is close to correct and the verdict concedes most of it: the record's own recheck is written to delete the code rather than to re-justify it. What holds it up for now is narrow, that the stdlib-only convention under tools/ is real and currently unbroken, and that the alternative is not 'add Pillow' but 'add the first third-party import this directory has ever had' for four watermark files.
_scope: Covers both files in tools/wsl as of 2026-08-03. The two share no code and are judged separately above; if either is deleted, this record must be re-scoped rather than inherited by the survivor.
